pool.text: Portuguese explorer Paulo Dias de Novais founded the city of Luanda.
The Portuguese constructed the fortress called Fortaleza São Pedro da Barra.
The fortress named Fortaleza de São Miguel was built in Luanda.
Between five thousand and ten thousand slaves were annually sold here.
The fortress called Forte de São Francisco do Penedo was built.
The slave trade was officially abolished in the region.
Luanda grew to a town containing sixty one thousand inhabitants.
The population of the cosmopolitan major city reached 475328.
Most of the white Portuguese left as refugees at the start.
The sports club changed its colonial related name.
A report famously called Luanda the Paris of Africa.
Provisional Angolan governments cleared the Boavista slum in Luanda Bay.
The first modern shopping mall in Angola was established.
The city began hosting the annual Luanda International Jazz Festival.
The province was enlarged by adding two additional municipalities.
New import tariffs imposed in March made Luanda expensive.
A scientific paper estimated future climate conditions using scenarios.
The IPCC report identified Luanda as severely affected by sea level.
António Agostinho Neto International Airport finally opened in November.
The population reached more than 8.8 million inhabitants.
